topology: R1 Gi0/0 192.0.2.1/24 directly connected to PC1 Gi0 192.0.2.10/24; PC gateway 192.0.2.1. Addressing and startup baselines are provided. No routing protocol or authentication server is needed.
verificationNotes: Practice starts at zero credit with no users, enable secret, console login policy or SSH service. The reference configures admin privilege 15 and operator privilege 1 with local secrets, a separate enable secret, console login local, domain name, 2048-bit RSA keys, SSH version 2 and local/SSH-only VTY 0–4.

Six live configuration goals are separate from one genuine echo goal and two successful local SSH login achievements. The completed reference earns only the six configuration goals; it does not prepopulate login, session or traffic evidence.

PC1 uses the existing Windows SSH client through the packet engine. Incorrect and case-mismatched passwords fail; a password prompt or TCP connection is not sufficient for login credit. The initial authenticated privilege must match the planned account.

The operator begins at R1> and level 1, cannot enter configuration mode, and needs the independent enable secret to reach R1# and level 15. Its own user password and a configured legacy enable password cannot substitute for the enable secret. The administrator begins directly at level 15.

Fresh console sessions require Username and hidden Password prompts. Wrong credentials return to authentication. The original provisioning console remains usable while login local is applied; saving and reloading the workspace provides a fresh console test without changing the topology.

Readonly local SSH evidence is recorded only after accepted non-AAA login local authentication, with target runtime, source address, username, assigned initial privilege, line and time. It is bounded to 1000 records and exposes copied records without passwords. Closing a connection retains evidence; replacing the runtime invalidates that transient evidence.

Lesson achievements retain successful login/echo observations across session exit and saved-lab reopening, using the existing bounded observations format. Local user and access settings stay live: deleting an account or disabling the required VTY transport removes configuration credit even when login achievements were previously earned.

Local user grading requires an explicitly named account with a nonempty secret and the intended privilege. Shared password fields and inherited account names do not substitute. VTY grading checks coverage of 0–4, accepts a safe 0–15 range, and rejects bypasses or extra enabled Telnet listeners. AAA configuration is outside this non-AAA lab.

Negative tests include missing keys, disabled transport, Telnet refusal, lost links, wrong privileges, shared-line authentication, AAA method lists and fake runtime/log entries. These cannot fabricate the required local login evidence.

All published IOS and Windows verification commands are exercised. The existing show ssh notice for no SSHv1/SSHv2 connections is classified as informational, rather than a parser failure. Authentication decisions and networking behavior are otherwise unchanged.

Startup reboot uses saved credentials and discards transient login/session records. Portable reload preserves earned guide observations but reconstructs fresh console/SSH sessions, rather than serializing ready sessions. Credentials remain ordinary simulated configuration data; no new cryptographic implementation is claimed.

Browser scenarios run serially in isolated persistent profiles against identical local HTML. Both themes at 1440, 390 and 320 pixels cover provisioning, wrong passwords, privilege denial/elevation, hidden input, actual show users/ssh, ping, transport refusal/recovery, saved reload, console reauthentication and completed-reference save/cancel flows.

Host/path/query-preserving permalink tests return to Services & Security with an accessible singular count of one lab. Generic catalog checks cover group/section counts, existing routing labs, offline operation, save/cancel protection and guide prerequisites.

Desktop topology and light/dark mobile guides were visually reviewed. The generated stylesheet is byte-for-byte unchanged, preserving the existing UI and console appearance. No live CML validation or external AAA feature expansion is claimed.
unitChecks: local-auth practice is independent, zero-credit and has two addressed nodes without users or SSH
published IOS configuration and completed reference earn six live goals and require two real logins plus a ping
fresh console prompts for a username and hidden password, rejects unknown/bad credentials and applies local privileges
SSH rejects a bad password without login credit and only accepts the matching case-sensitive local user secret
privilege-1 SSH cannot configure until the independent enable secret is supplied, and disable returns to user EXEC
an enable secret takes precedence over a configured legacy enable password
removing login local or allowing Telnet loses live VTY credit and cannot create local-SSH login evidence
missing RSA keys or disabled VTY transport prevents real SSH even with valid user configuration
the SSH-only configuration refuses Telnet and a lost link prevents new SSH without undoing earned login credit
login evidence is scoped to target, source, username and initial privilege; fake runtime/log entries cannot earn credit
local accounts with a shared password field or inherited names cannot earn the required secret-based user goal
wrong privilege cannot earn the planned account or login goal, even when SSH successfully authenticates
AAA method-list authentication does not substitute for the non-AAA line configuration or local-SSH evidence
accepted login evidence is read-only, excludes passwords and is not serialized as a ready session
saved-lab reload keeps achieved logins and ping while live config remains required and a fresh console authenticates again
startup reboot reconstructs authentication from saved settings and discards transient login evidence
VTY coverage accepts a safe 0–15 range but rejects missing lines, bypasses and extra Telnet listeners
imported local-auth criteria are bounded declarative data and reject invalid privileges, settings or identifiers
all published show and Windows verification commands report working local access and actual sessions
